newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss consumer confidence index up slightly -govt.
newsitem.headline: Swiss consumer confidence index up slightly -govt.

text.p: Swiss consumer confidence recovered slightly but remained at low levels in the three months to October, marking the first upturn in over a year, the Swiss Federal Office for Economic Issues said.
It said that consumer expectations also improved, although the nation continued to worry about job security.

It said the index, in the latest survey, rose to a level of minus 38 from a level of minus 41 points in the comparable period ending in July. The latest reading marks the first upturn in the index since April 1995.
The index measures current sentiment, as well as households' past and expected future financial situations.
It is expressed as the net difference between positive and negative answers in a quarterly poll of roughly 1,000 households.

Job security remained a major worry, with the index sinking to a minus 145 points in October from a minus 137 in July. The jobs component was thus close to its all-time low of minus 150 points measured in October 1992.
"But the future economic situation was viewed as significantly less pessimistic," the Federal Office said.
It said that households also viewed the present time as "less unfavourable" for major purchases, and judged their financial situation as unchanged.
However, the number of households which were able to save money declined slightly, the Federal Office said.
